questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Pump your brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes helps your car stop quickly in an emergency. It also lets you keep control of the steering.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll into the curb and not into traffic.

questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go.
Stop, look in all directions, then go.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, you must yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield by taking your foot off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circular traffic light. Traffic in the arrow's direction must stop and cannot turn that way.

questions.question: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be within ____ of the curb.

options.text: 10 inches
12 inches
18 inches
24 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches
questions.explanation: When parallel parking, park your wheels parallel to and 12 inches away from the curb. Park only where you do not block traffic and other drivers can see your car clearly.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow mean?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look for other vehicles, then go if safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system do?

options.text: Make your engine use too much oil.
Mean you need a tune-up sooner.
Make you drowsy while driving.
Start fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from your engine. A leak can release poisonous fumes that may make you drowsy while driving and can be dangerous.

questions.question: What must you do to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: Do not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are good.
The speed suggested for driving on a road when conditions are good.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are good. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones and work zones. If bad weather or road construction makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if it starts to move. On a hill without a curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a green arrow at a traffic light?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in the direction of the arrow. You must be in the correct lane to make the turn. Always let other vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells drivers that there is low clearance ahead.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see enough of the road to stay safe until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Drive around a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels will keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop when stopping on:

options.text: A wet or icy road.
Paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads. They also increase on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out and look behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors. This is especially important when children are nearby.

questions.question: In good weather and traffic, what is the minimum distance you should stay behind another car?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum distance of three seconds behind other cars in normal weather and traffic. This gives you time to react. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: You should signal to turn ____ before beginning the turn.

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
20 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use your turn signal or arm signal to tell other drivers what you plan to do. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and check if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you know it is not coming toward you.
